claims.statement: The permissions reusable limits larger runners to organizations and enterprises on Team or GitHub Enterprise Cloud plans. Frontmatter listing GHES is not support evidence; the body has a separate GHES unsupported branch.
For GHES, the reusable recommends self-hosted runners and explicitly states GitHub-hosted runners are unsupported. The source directs readers to Enterprise Cloud documentation about larger runners.

In the non-GHES branch, the include describes GitHub-managed virtual machines with preinstalled tools and more RAM/CPU/disk, static IPs, grouping, autoscaling and GPU runners; Azure networking is feature-gated inside that include.
All larger runners in this branch support runner groups controlling repository access, demand-based autoscaling, and job concurrency limits.
Static IP ranges for firewall allowlists, custom images and Azure private networking are limited here to Linux and Windows runners; these are not universal platform claims.

Under default-setup-larger-runners (fpt/ghec), consider larger runners for code-scanning default setup when standard scans are slow, hit memory/disk errors, or require size/image/concurrency customization without self-hosting. This is conditional recommendation rather than mandatory configuration.

Larger runners never use included private-repository minutes and are billed per executed minute in both public/private repositories. The include states unused configured larger runners incur no workflow execution charge; rates themselves are only linked, not asserted.
Manage/reference links are next steps; the final conditional terminator preserves non-GHES applicability. No runner was created, started, billed or configured.
